findings.F1: Across all coins on a non-overlapping 5-day grid, the bars the detector marked as breakouts ("trending") were followed by a 5-day move +1.81 % above the coin's normal drift (t 2.72, 217 cases), while all other bars gave -0.12 % (t -0.62, 3202 cases), so the level break carries the effect.
findings.F2: Inside those breakouts, the rise does not grow with distance above the 50-day average: Spearman -0.043 on raw distance and -0.007 on volatility-scaled distance (217 cases). By distance tercile the unusual 5-day move is +1.18 % (t 1.07), +4.61 % (t 2.40) and +0.80 % (t 0.51), at mean distances of 2.8 %, 7.0 % and 15.6 %. This is why the slope check failed.
findings.F3: The book's trades run against its own sizing: mean net profit per trade falls from 6.07 % in the lowest entry-forecast quintile to 0.93 % in the highest, with medians of +0.87 % and -0.59 % (224 trades each).
findings.F4: After a day whose rise is large against the coin's 20-day volatility (top fifth), the next 5 days beat the coin's normal drift by +1.63 % (t 3.24, 570 cases). The other four fifths range from -0.65 % to +0.02 %, and the overall Spearman is only 0.022 (2843 cases), so the effect sits in the largest days, not along a slope.
findings.F6: The book's best 5 % of days come after the coin rose 17.5 % over 5 days and 29.8 % over 20 days; its worst 5 % come after -0.6 % over 5 days and +8.6 % over 20 days (233 days each). The book earns when the break is already part of a sharp run, and loses when the break comes without one.
findings.F7: Weekday daily returns reach t 3.76 (Saturday +0.30 %) and t -2.70 (Thursday -0.30 %) pooled. Per coin, only 3 of 42 cells pass |t| 2.3, so with this many angles examined I do not count it as a finding to build on.

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, it tends to keep rising over the next 5 days, and the more it rose over the past 5 days against its own 20-day volatility, the larger that rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size level breaks by the sharpness of the run that carried price through the level, not by how far price stands above its average.
ideas.name: breakout graded by run sharpness

ideas.idea: After a day on which a coin rises by much more than its 20-day volatility, it tends to keep rising over the next 5 days, and the larger that day's rise relative to its volatility, the larger the 5-day rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long after a coin's unusually large up days and refuse to fade them over the following week.
ideas.name: large up day continues
